title: I Forwarded the Group Vacation Spreadsheet to the Person Paying Nothing

parts.text: I opened the shared sheet at 9:17 p.m. and watched Derek add a hot tub upgrade while his contribution column stayed a hyphen. Six of us were going to Asheville. I was thirty-one, the one who had put down the deposit with a card that still had dentist residue. The group chat said we were all equal. The sheet said I had paid eighteen hundred and Derek had paid a vibe. I added a tab titled WHO ACTUALLY PAID. I did not @ him. I turned on edit history. At 9:41 Derek wrote, "Don't make it weird, I'll Venmo later." Later had been eleven months of later since Mexico. Then he booked a spa slot under my name so it would hit my card on file.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He booked a spa on my card while his contribution cell is still a hyphen.

social.video_title: He upgraded the hot tub and paid a hyphen — Part 1/2
social.description: Asheville deposit, a spreadsheet with a vibe column, and a spa booking on my card. Would you have locked the sheet?

parts.text: I removed my card from the booking, forwarded the WHO ACTUALLY PAID tab to the group, and set the sheet to comment-only. Derek called me controlling. Two friends paid me within an hour. Derek paid nothing and dropped out, which is the first honest cell he ever filled. We kept the cabin without the hot tub upgrade. Asheville smelled like woodsmoke and cheap coffee. I ate pancakes without calculating his hyphen. The dentist card recovered. The group chat made a new rule: no names on bookings without money in the column first. I enforced it by existing.

social.video_title: I took my card off and made the sheet comment-only — Part 2/2
social.description: Edit history, a spa ambush, and friends who can read a column. Was a vibe ever a deposit?
